context:
Goal: a lane cannot pass its own lint by loosening the check that judges it, and a lane that fixes a check is never stuck.
Problem (rule): lane lint (the check run on a lane's branch before it merges) runs the lane's own copy of any lint file it changed, so a lane that loosens a check and its test together passes; a builder made it use main's copy, and a reviewer found that this fails honest lanes that change code and re-point a test, so a rule must give way and only you can say which.
Based on (read): an Explore read of merge/merge.py lines 3504 to 3511 and bin/ci-job line 662, 20:31 CST: lane lint runs the lane's copy of a changed lint file.
Based on (measured): the round-1 reviewer on branch lane/check-judged-by-main-copy, 20:56 CST: 53 of the last 150 main commits touch a file that lane lint judges, and a lane that changes code and re-points its test fails against main's old test.
Departs from: main — lane lint judges the lane's copy of a changed check — b and c change it to main's copy for all changed checks or for lint checks only.
Waiting on: nothing stopped; step check-judged-by-main-copy waits on your pick (the reviewer's other two findings are fixed by a builder either way).

options.gain: No lane is ever stuck on lane lint.
options.how: No change; the builder's branch is dropped.
options.label: Keep lane lint as it is: it judges the lane's own copy of a changed check
options.lose: A lane that loosens a check and its test together still passes its own lane lint (a mistake the reviewer must catch by reading the diff).

options.gain: A lane cannot pass by loosening the check that judges it.
options.how: The builder's branch as it stands: main's version of each changed lint file and hooks test file runs at lane lint.
options.label: Judge every changed check and test file by main's copy
options.lose: A lane that changes code and re-points its test is judged by the old test and fails; 53 of the last 150 main commits touch such a file; a fix to a broken check cannot pass until main has it.

options.gain: The loosened-check hole closes for the checks, and a lane that re-points a test is not stuck.
options.how: A builder narrows the laying to lint/*.py check files; hooks/test_*.py suites keep the lane's copy, as they are re-pointed with their code.
options.label: Judge only changed lint/*.py check files by main's copy; tests stay the lane's (recommended)
options.lose: A lane that loosens only a test still passes lane lint; a fix to a broken lint check is still judged by the broken copy and needs the solo merge route.

ref: owner chat 19:45 CST Nov 17 (relayed by the consultant): land the verification article's findings
reply: You are right that c is a bandaid. The larger problem: a check can be loosened in the same change that is judged by it, so the check proves nothing about itself. Choosing a copy to run (a, b or c) only moves where the hole sits. My proposal, not yet a ruling, and unmeasured: judge a changed check by outcome. A lane that changes a check must show the check still fails the defect it was built for (the red run on its fixture, rule verification-trust-guard-after-red), and a changed check gets a reviewer who reads its diff first (rule roles-review-cap-three already puts a guard or check change under the net-value test). That needs no copy rule, fails no honest lane that re-points a test, and catches a loosened check by its behavior. Cost: each check needs a recorded failing fixture; I have not counted how many lack one. Say 'a holistic fix' and I turn it into a step and re-ask a smaller question; I have not changed the item's options.
short: Lane lint: judge changed checks by main's copy?

shown.label: Keep lane lint as it is: it judges the lane's own copy of a changed check
Judge every changed check and test file by main's copy
Judge only changed lint/*.py check files by main's copy; tests stay the lane's (recommended)

title: Should lane lint judge a changed check by main's copy, knowing a lane that re-points a test can then fail it?
why: c closes the hole where a check judges itself without failing the common lane that re-points a test with its code; a leaves the hole, b fails the lanes behind about 1 in 3 main commits. Recommended by triage, not owner-typed.
